advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an 'ahead of' relation for the merge_base == tip case so the stale message names it accurately.
evidence: In tip mode a tree that contains the tip has merge_base == tip (not head), so relation resolves to 'diverged from' though it is actually ahead
advisory.finding: _stale_lines labels any non-behind stale tree as 'diverged from', including an ahead-of-tip tree in tip mode (merge_base == tip, i.e. HEAD strictly contains the tip). Such a tree is 'ahead of', not 'diverged from', the tracked tip; the message is misleading for that case.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move `id-token: write` from the workflow top-level `permissions:` to the `plan` job's own `permissions:` block (keeping `contents: read` where needed), matching reconcile-bridge.yml/structured-output-baseline.yml/release.yml.
evidence: terraform-drift.yml:48-50 `permissions:\n  id-token: write   # required for OIDC AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity\n  contents: read`

The `plan` job (terraform-drift.yml:76-81) declares no `permissions:` block, so it inherits the workflow-wide `id-token: write`; only the `fmt` job scopes down with its own `permissions: contents: read` (lines 57-58).

reconcile-bridge.yml:83 comment: `# Job-level for the same reason structured-output-baseline.yml puts it there.` establishes that OIDC `id-token: write` is granted per-job in this repo, not workflow-wide.
release.yml:435 `id-token: write` is also scoped at the job level.
advisory.finding: `id-token: write` is granted at the workflow top-level (permissions: default) rather than scoped to the single `plan` job that assumes the OIDC role, diverging from the repo's established job-level OIDC convention; the `plan` job declares no `permissions:` block and inherits the elevated token, so any future job added without its own block also silently inherits OIDC minting rights.
scenarios: A future job (e.g. an apply step, a notifier) is added to terraform-drift.yml without its own permissions block and silently gains the ability to mint an OIDC token and assume rebar-terraform-plan.
advisory.suggested_fix: Set top-level `permissions: contents: read` only, and add a job-level `permissions:` block to `plan` granting `id-token: write` and `contents: read`. This removes the need for `fmt` to redundantly re-scope and prevents future jobs from inheriting OIDC rights by default.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 349 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug fd2b-7af3-3d6e-48cf has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan fd2b-7af3-3d6e-48cf` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review fd2b-7af3-3d6e-48cf` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan fd2b-7af3-3d6e-48cf --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
